BonviniKennedyKeele2023MinimaxSubgroup: supplies the level-set model and uses causal simulation laws, but not this exact augmented uniform-cube transverse witness with its tight lower-margin calculation.

repo_prior_art.cite: No in-catalogue Stat entry proves a matched CATE level-set minimax rate in the calibrated \(\xi\gamma>d\) transverse regime.

published_prior_art.cite: BonviniKennedyKeele2023MinimaxSubgroup: Corollary 1 gives the upper rate, while Theorem 1 restricts its converse to \(\xi\gamma\le d\) and explicitly leaves a tight lower bound without that restriction open.

BonviniKennedyKeele2023MinimaxSubgroup and AudibertTsybakov2007FastPlugin constrain crossing geometry but do not characterize the nonempty causal \((\xi,\gamma)\) frontier or its two-branch minimax rate.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:transverse-minimax-rate
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The achievability transfer is confined to fixed calibrated \(\kappa\), where the exact two-sided density constants force the known uniform design; it is not asserted for generic bounded-density designs.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The matched \((r_n^*)^2\) rate is claimed over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{tr}}(\gamma;\kappa)\) for fixed calibrated \(\kappa\) and \(\gamma>d\).

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 9–11, Definition 4, Lemma 3, Corollary 1, Theorem 1, and the paragraph immediately following Theorem 1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Definition 4 specifies the local CATE/nuisance smoothness model and matrix conditions; Lemma 3 is conditional on density-ratio, matrix, and approximation conditions; Corollary 1 gives \(r_n^{*\,1+\xi}\); Theorem 1 imposes \(\xi\gamma\le d\), and the paper states that a tight lower bound without that condition remains open.
The paper derives minimax CATE rates in a Hölder-smooth nonparametric model using localized fuzzy hypotheses and presents a local-polynomial R-learner under high-level regularity conditions.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Proposition 3.4, as identified and applied in BonviniKennedyKeele2023MinimaxSubgroup p. 5
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited classification result supplies the Hölder-margin interior-crossing obstruction used to diagnose feasible super-margin regimes; it does not supply the proposed causal minimax converse.

The paper studies plug-in density-level-set estimation under local smoothness and a margin-type exponent and gives minimax lower bounds, making it an adjacent noncausal analogue rather than a result on observational CATE level sets.

The paper formulates regression subgroup selection as constrained optimization over low-complexity sets with a guaranteed-probability/Type-I-error constraint, distinct from unrestricted weighted CATE symmetric-difference risk.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Extend the upper-bound verification and converse beyond the exactly uniform calibrated cube to a named nonuniform known- or estimable-density subclass, with explicit density-ratio and local-Gram control.

Turn the frontier OEQ into an iff feasibility theorem: characterize all interior-crossing \((\xi,\gamma)\) pairs under the stated two-sided-density model and give witnesses or impossibility proofs for each region.
Add a boundary corollary showing explicitly how the transverse \(\xi=1\) result meets the \(\gamma\downarrow d\) edge of the Bonvini--Kennedy--Keele lower-bound regime.

recommended_next_step: Advance the calibrated transverse converse to Stage 0 as a field-tier solve target; retain the nontransverse frontier as the follow-on open problem.
